page_description: Explore macroeconomics through real data, interactive models, Python notebooks, and AI podcasts. A companion by Carlos Mendez.

slides.question:
Why are some countries
so much richer?
slides.description: Start with the differences in living standards. Then ask what capital, ideas, and institutions can explain.
slides.alt: GDP per person for the United States, Japan, China, and India from 1950 to 2022.

slides.question:
Why do economies
fall into recession?
slides.description: Follow output through financial crises and the pandemic. See how far an economy can move from its potential.
slides.source: Data · U.S. output gap · BEA / CBO via FRED
slides.alt: U.S. output relative to potential, including the financial crisis and pandemic.

slides.question:
What drives
inflation?
slides.description: Trace the history of rising prices, then connect money, expectations, and policy to the inflation rate.
slides.alt: Annual U.S. consumer price inflation from 1960 through 2025.

slides.question:
Why does
unemployment persist?
slides.description: Even in a growing economy, jobs are created and lost. A simple flow model explains a persistent natural rate.
slides.source: Model · Job separation 1% · job finding 20% / month
slides.alt: Unemployment converges from 10 percent to a natural rate of 4.76 percent over 24 months.

slides.question:
How can policy
stabilize the economy?
slides.description: Bring inflation and output into one diagram. Explore the trade-offs facing central banks after a shock.
slides.alt: Aggregate supply and demand intersect at a zero output gap and 2 percent inflation.

slides.question:
How do trade and exchange
rates connect economies?
slides.description: Follow prices and interest rates across borders. Explore how international connections reshape domestic choices.
slides.source: Model · Uncovered interest parity · one-year horizon
slides.alt: The exchange rate rises with the domestic interest rate, holding foreign interest and expected exchange rates fixed.

pillars_html:
THREE PILLARS. ONE CONNECTED APPROACH.

From evidence
to explanation.

Find a pattern. Build an explanation.
Use AI to go further—and check every step.

  1. 01 / DATA SCIENCE

    From data to facts

    Download, plot, and explore real economic data. Compare countries and periods to discover which patterns hold—and which questions to ask next.

    Explore Data Apps ↗
  2. 02 / MACROECONOMIC MODELS

    From facts to models

    Operate the models that explain the facts. Move a slider, change a parameter, and compare the prediction with what the data show.

    Explore Figure Apps ↗
  3. 03 / AI-POWERED LEARNING

    AI-powered learning

    Work with an AI assistant in Colab, see the big picture in mind maps and slides, and learn by changing the code. Use AI, but check its answers.

    Start with Python and AI ↗
